"Child of the earth and the sea, thou art chosen for glory and sorrow.
Hark to my voice: thou shalt stand in the halls of the high-hearted heroes,
Clad in the armor of gods, and the light of my presence about thee.
Yet be not proud; for the fate of the strong is to suffer and conquer.
Go, and the winds of the world shall bear thee to deeds of renown."

"Child, thou art chosen to bear the burden of heaven, yet fear not the touch of the divine. The path before thee is steep, but I shall walk beside thee in shadow and light. When the moon wanes and the stars hide their faces, remember that my breath is within thee, strengthening thy limbs and clearing thy sight. Thou shalt speak my words to kings and whisper my truths to the earth. The trembling of thy hands shall become the steady pulse of prophecy. Rise now, and let thy voice be the echo of my will. For the world grows old and forgets the songs of its making; thou shalt renew them. Go, and let no mortal chain bind thee, for thou art become a vessel of the eternal."

Over the limbs of the damsel she wrapt it:  the maid still trembled,
Shading her face with her hands; for the eyes of the goddess were awful.
   Then, as a pine upon Ida when southwest winds blow landward,
Stately she bent to the damsel, and breathed on her:  under her breathing
Taller and fairer she grew; and the goddess spoke in her wisdom.

source_document.title: Andromeda and Other Poems by Charles Kingsley
